expectations.text: Produces options that differ in mechanism rather than being variations on 'make the meeting more engaging'
expectations.evidence: Mechanism spread is real if narrower: move status content to a written pre-read, put a live decision at stake, anonymous upvoted Q&A, halve the length, rotate who presents, change the cadence to quarterly, delay the recording. Cadence, recording policy and content relocation are mechanism changes, not engagement tweaks.

expectations.text: At least one option questions the premise — whether the all-hands should exist in this form, or whether attendance is the right thing to optimise
expectations.evidence: 'Try a different cadence. Monthly is an awkward interval ... Quarterly-but-excellent plus a strong written monthly update beats a mediocre monthly ritual. This is worth considering seriously rather than treating cadence as fixed.' Also questions optimising attendance itself: 'Attendance is a useful thermometer; don't break the thermometer.'

expectations.text: Does not treat declining attendance as purely a content-quality problem
expectations.evidence: Opens 'Falling all-hands attendance is almost always a symptom, not the problem' and splits causes into value, stakes and friction — two of the three are not content quality.

expectations.text: Proportionate: under roughly 800 words, no heavy scaffolding for a light question
expectations.evidence: wc -w = 604 words, under ~800. No scaffolding: four short bolded sections and a closing question.

expectations.text: MODE CHECK: did NOT spawn parallel generator subagents or run web research for this
expectations.evidence: metrics.json: subagents_spawned 0, web_searches 0, total_tool_calls 3. user_notes.md: 'No research, no subagents, no web searches.'

expectations.text: Surfaces at least one non-obvious diagnosis of WHY attendance falls, not just a list of fixes
expectations.evidence: 'look at *who* is missing. If it's clustered by team or time zone, it's friction. If it's spread evenly and skews senior, it's value. If newer people attend and long-tenured people don't, it's "I've seen this movie ten times".' Also: 'recording always available so live attendance is strictly dominated.'
